text:
Tuesday in Vegas, the Golden Knights led 3-1 and then didn't. Dallas came back to win 4-3 in overtime, helped by what Jesse Granger called a "fortunate bounce" that found Wyatt Johnston at the back door to make it 3-2 with 1:18 to play. Two nights later the teams do it again in the same building, the last game of a five-game Vegas home stand.

Vegas has the better argument with the chances. The Golden Knights are winless in three (0-1-2) and outscored 13-8, but with 54% of the expected goals (the quality of the chances) in those games, and 56% over their last five. That's what bad luck looks like, though it won't feel that way to a team that gave up a two-goal lead at home. Victor Olofsson has been their best story: 11 points in his last 10, and earned, since he's getting more and better shots than usual. Mitch Marner is one assist from 600 and has a 10-game home point streak. Adin Hill starts again (+2.0 saves above expected this season after -15.0 last year). Noah Hanifin is out.

The Stars have won three straight, 8-4 in goals, but our numbers say only half of that is them: 53% of the chances, with the goaltending saving 3.9 goals more than expected. Jake Oettinger, who won Tuesday, starts again; he is at +7.7 this season, among the reasons Dallas sits at 87% to make the playoffs in our simulations. Jamie Benn just became the second fifth-round pick ever to reach 1,000 points, and Johnston has goals in three straight. Oskar Bäck and Tyler Myers are out.

Our numbers have it close: 2.96 expected goals for Vegas, 2.78 for Dallas. Johnston (36%) and Jason Robertson (35%) lead the Stars to score; Mark Stone (34%) leads Vegas.
headline: Stars and Golden Knights, take two in two days
